paper.title_en: Thermoelasticity-induced interferometer-displacement noise from the test mass in spaceborne gravitational-wave detectors
paper.abstract_en: In spaceborne gravitational-wave detectors, the test mass is treated as an ideal rigid end mirror for interferometric-displacement readout. In reality, however, as a thermoelastic body, it deforms under radiative heating from the surrounding electrode housing, shifting the effective laser-reflection point and coupling into displacement noise. In this work, we develop a coupled model of radiative heating, thermoelastic deformation, and laser sensing and derive an analytical expression relating housing temperature fluctuations to displacement noise. Applying TianQin parameters, the result shows that a displacement noise allocation of <math display="inline"><mn>0.1</mn><mtext>  </mtext><mi>pm</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>Hz</mi></msqrt></math> requires electrode-housing temperature fluctuations below <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>43</mn><mtext>  </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>Hz</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> at <math display="inline"><mn>0.1</mn><mrow><mtext>  </mtext><mi>mHz</mi></mrow></math> and <math display="inline"><mn>430</mn><mtext>  </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>Hz</mi></msqrt></math> at <math display="inline"><mn>1</mn><mrow><mtext>  </mtext><mi>mHz</mi></mrow></math>.
